## Case Study 1

## Option 1: Development Psychology
You work as a research assistant in a developmental psychology lab at UT. You’ve recently
been assigned to work with one of the lab’s graduate students on a large-scale cross-cultural
study, where children at many sites across the world completed a series of experimental tasks.
The graduate student is making a poster to show off their preliminary work and would like your
help with the descriptive analysis portion.

You will focus on just one task from the larger battery, where children watched an adult build a
tower out of special blocks and were subsequently asked to build their own tower. The adult’s
tower had 10 distinctive features and each child’s tower was given an imitation score (0-10)
based on how many of those features they incorporated into their own tower. Each child’s age
was also recorded.

![Dataset for Option 1](assets/case_study_1_option_1_devsci.csv){.filelink}

## Option 2: Cognitive Psychology
You work as a research assistant in a cognition lab at UT. You’ve recently been assigned to
work with one of the lab’s graduate students on a memory study. The graduate student is
making a poster to show off their preliminary work and would like your help with the descriptive
analysis portion.

Participants were assigned to one of two memory conditions (recognition or free recall) and had
to study one of two lists of words, one made of low frequency words (e.g. mercurial) in the
English language and one with high frequency words (e.g. dog). Each participant was assigned
to a single combination of memory and word frequency conditions. After studying the list of
words, participants in the recognition memory condition had to indicate if a subset of the old
words presented to them (along with an equal number of new words) was on the list or not,
while participants in the free recall condition had to write down as many words from the list as
they could remember. The number of correct responses was recorded for each participant.
Because each list consists of 50 total words, participants could get between 0 and 50 correct
responses.

![Dataset for Option 1](assets/case_study_1_option_2_cogsci.csv){.filelink}

## Rubric

Overall:
1. Sections: 
- Research Question and Hypotheses
- Methods Overview
- Results and Interpretation
- External sources
1. Submit an html file that is formatted well and organized logically.

Research Question and Hypotheses
- Research question (1 sentence)
- The main hypothesis (1 sentence)
- The null hypothesis (1 sentence)

Methods Overview
Explain how the the research question informs your methdological choices, like what groups you are comparing, what statistical procedues you are conducting, what plots your are creating, etc.

Results and Interpretation
1. At least one descriptive plot
1. At least one inferential plot
1. At least one summary table.
1. A main paragraph that includes:
    - Key results (means, sd, confidence intervals)
    - Appropriate interpretations for each result (don't "over-interpret")
    - Appropriate interpretations for each plot (don't "over-interpret")
    - As part of your interpretations, make sure to demonstrate an understanding of the definition of key concepts. Especially for:
        - Confidence interval
        - "Significance"
1. Using your own best judgment, how strongly do you think your results support the main hypothesis? Why?

External sources section:
The case studies can be completed without using any external sources. However, if you choose to use them, you must be able to justify the choice. So, please list every line of code and statistical concept that we have not covered in class, and explain:
1. What they do or mean
1. Why you have chosen to use this in place of what we learned in class
1. A link to the source, if it exists, otherwise a description is fine.
